newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.S. diplomat to administer U.N.-run Croatia enclave.
newsitem.headline: U.S. diplomat to administer U.N.-run Croatia enclave.

text.p: Former U.S. diplomat William Walker has been appointed as the new U.N. transitional administrator for Eastern Slavonia, a heavily Serb region of Croatia being returned to Zagreb's control, the United Nations announced on Wednesday.

Walker, most recently vice-president of the U.S. National Defence University, will take up his new post on Aug. 1, Secretary-General Kofi Annan said in a letter informing the Security Council of his decision.

Walker, 62, succeeds another American, Jacques Paul Klein, who administered Eastern Slavonia until his recent appointment as deputy to the chief international representative in Bosnia, Carlos Westendorp of Spain.
The U.N. Transitional Administration for Eastern Slavonia (UNTAES) has been governing the region in accordance with the 1995 Balkan peace accords, to ensure its smooth reintegration into Croatia.

The Security Council this month renewed the mandate of UNTAES until Jan. 15, 1998, and approved arrangements for winding down the operation and gradually witrhdrawing its 5,000 troops and other personnel.
Walker spent 34 years as a foreign service officer, serving in Peru, Japan, Brazil, El Salvador, Honduras and Bolivia.
He was ambassdador to El Salvador from August 1988 to March 1992 after serving as deputy assistant secretary of state for inter-American affairs.
